title: Textract vs PaddleOCR for Financial Tables: Why Table-Specific Tuning Won
excerpt: A six-layout financial OCR case study showing when managed table extraction works, when layout-specific tuning matters, and how to measure accuracy without overstating it.
seoTitle: Textract vs PaddleOCR for Financial Table OCR
seoDescription: Compare AWS Textract and PaddleOCR for dense financial tables through a six-layout OCR case study, architecture, accuracy framework, and production checklist.
author: Anoop Karnik

cover.prompt: Create one 16:9 editorial technology illustration for a Bayesian Labs engineering article about extracting structured financial tables from screenshots. claimNotes: The 100%, below-95%, and approximately-99.9% accuracy figures are builder-reported project validation results; the original labeled set and execution logs were not retained.
The roughly 750 visible fields count comes from the six supplied sample screens.
The 20–40 minute and 50–80% handling-time ranges are scenario estimates, not measured client KPIs.
Textract is not described as universally non-customizable; current AWS query adapters are acknowledged and distinguished from detector-level parameter tuning.
Do not publish the supplied Bloomberg terminal screenshots, workflow identifiers, spreadsheet identifiers, credentials references, or market values.
